extracted.intended_audience: eighteenth-century British political readers and policymakers (members of Parliament, financiers, and the informed public)
extracted.subtask_description: A critical political essay that evaluates a proposed peace establishment and accompanying financial schemes, exposing weaknesses in estimates, asserted savings, revenue proposals, and the political feasibility of taxation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: justify_changes_in_estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless you assign reasons for the increase or diminution of the several articles of public charge, the playing at establishments and estimates is an amusement of no higher order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposer must give reasons for every increase or decrease in items of public charge; merely presenting altered totals or speculative schemes without article-by-article justification is inadequate. The critic expects the author to explain why particular articles differ from previous estimates and to support such changes with argument or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: use_present_estimates_as_base_and_show_defalcations
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural method in a plan of reformation would be, to take the present existing estimates as they stand; and then to show what may be practicably and safely defalcated from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sound financial proposal should start from current, realistic estimates and then demonstrate what can safely be reduced. Inventing a separate 'ideal' estimate and claiming reductions relative to that is misleading; the proposer should show practical, provable cuts from the real baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: compare_projects_article_by_article
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not from anything our author has anywhere said, that you are enabled to find the ground, much less the justification, of the immense difference between these several systems; you must compare them yourself, article by article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple proposed schemes or prior plans exist, the author should present a clear article-by-article comparison, explaining the rationale for each variance. Leaving readers to do this comparison is a failure of exposition and justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: do_not_claim_savings_on_hopes_or_speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Such is the whole of this mighty scheme. ... He _hopes_, _mights_, _insinuations_, _expectations_, and _inducements_ ... If any of these Hopes, Mights, Insinuations, Expectations, and Inducements, should fail him, there will be a formidable gaping breach in his whole project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Savings or new revenues must be evidenced and actionable; they cannot be treated as credible merely because the proposer 'hopes' or 'expects' them. The essay provides numerical examples showing claimed savings far exceed plausible, specified items—claiming large aggregate reductions on the basis of small or speculative items is criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: specify_what_will_be_cut_in_military_services
rubrics_metrics.description: It is incumbent on him to let us know, not what sums he will cut off, but what branch of that service he deems superfluous. Instead of putting us off with unmeaning generalities, he ought to have stated what naval force, what naval works, and what naval stores, with the lowest estimated expense, are necessary...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing reductions in sensitive services (e.g., the navy or army), the proposer must identify the exact branches, works, or stores to be reduced, and justify that those cuts will preserve essential capability. Aggregate numbers without such specification are unacceptable, especially for services where under-provision carries grave risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: account_for_non_annual_and_longer_term_charges
rubrics_metrics.description: A year's estimate is therefore no just idea at all of a permanent peace establishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial planning for a 'peace establishment' must consider charges that are non-annual or irregular (stock purchases, large works, intermittent supplies). One-year snapshots mislead; proposals should be evaluated over a reasonable multi-year term to account for fluctuating and deferred costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ground_calculations_on_conservative_averages
rubrics_metrics.description: He should ground his speculation rather on the lowest mediums because all new schemes are known to be subject to some defect or failure; and which therefore every prudent proposer will be ready to allow for, in order to lay his foundation as low and as solid as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conservative (lower) averages or cautious baselines when projecting savings and revenues. Selecting unusually favorable years to make an account look good is an unsound practice; prudent financiers use indifferent or low mediums to allow for unforeseen defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: provide_local_detail_before_proposing_foreign_taxes
rubrics_metrics.description: When any man proposes new taxes in a country with which he is not personally conversant by residence or office, he ought to lay open its situation much more minutely and critically than this author has done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before proposing taxes on a foreign or colonial polity (Ireland, America), the proposer must analyze its entire economic and fiscal situation—trade, remittances, exchange, local establishments, debts, methods of taxation—and not infer ability to pay from a single increased trade item.

rubrics_metrics.name: explain_mode_and_proportions_of_collection_across_territories
rubrics_metrics.description: If he leaves it to themselves to settle these proportions, he adjourns it to doomsday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When imposing aggregate sums to be raised from many distinct provinces, the proposal must specify how the sum will be apportioned and collected (proportions, methods). Leaving apportionment vague or delegated without mechanism makes the revenue speculative and unenforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: demonstrate_how_revenues_will_be_compelled_or_induced
rubrics_metrics.description: Does he lay open any part of his plan how they may be compelled to pay it, without plunging ourselves into calamities that outweigh tenfold the proposed benefit? or does he show how they may be induced to submit to it quietly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A revenue proposal must explain measures for collection and enforcement that are politically and practically feasible. Listing theoretical revenue amounts without showing how to obtain them (or how to secure consent) is insufficient and misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: value_revenues_by_market_or_investor_assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Most moneyed men know their own interest right well; and are as able as any financier, in the valuation of risks. Yet I think this financier will scarcely find that adventurer hardy enough, at any premium, to advance a shilling upon a vote of such taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The credibility of a proposed revenue should be judged by whether an interested investor would accept it at realistic terms. If no prudent investor would underwrite such revenue, it is not 'real' money in practical terms; treating it as such is deceptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: do_not_rely_on_authority_instead_of_proof
rubrics_metrics.description: A man is generally rendered somewhat a worse reasoner for having been a minister... begging the question with impunity, and asserting without thinking himself obliged to prove.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments from authority or past office are inadequate substitutes for evidence and reasoning. Proposers must provide demonstrable proof for claims rather than rely on their reputation or former positions to carry assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid_crediting_temporary_or_time_dependent_savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the one and the other belong equally (as indeed all the rest do) to the present administration, to any administration; because they are the gift of time, and not the bounty of the exchequer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not count on savings that exist only because of timing (e.g., a fund limited to current beneficiaries, one-time reductions, completed surveys). Such intermittent or naturally declining charges cannot be reliably credited to a new administration's permanent economy plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: assess_political_feasibility_and_risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the author then seriously mean to propose in Parliament a land-tax ... upon Ireland? If he does ... he will throw the whole empire ... into mortal convulsions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial measures must be assessed for their political consequences—popular resistance, alienation of colonies or subordinate kingdoms, and the risk of provoking 'convulsions'. A plan that is technically possible but politically explosive is not a sound policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: ensure_arithmetic_consistency_but_prioritize_substantive_logic
rubrics_metrics.description: To what this strange inaccuracy [in arithmetic] is owing, I cannot possibly comprehend; nor is it very material, where the logic is so bad, and the policy so erroneous, whether the arithmetic be just or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While correct arithmetic is required and inaccuracies undermine credibility (examples of mismatched sums are given), the substantive logic and policy coherence are paramount; both should be present—accurate figures supported by sound reasoning.
